verdict.reasoning: Fatigue/low energy: "I don't have much energy at all during the day"; sleep disturbance: "I'm just having trouble sleeping at all"; poor concentration: "Finding it really hard to... keep focusing"; decreased appetite: "I'm not eating very much at the moment"; decreased libido: "my mood is lower recently and so I like my sex drive has kind of decreased"; shortness of breath on exertion: "when I've been doing sports as well, I find sometimes it's quite difficult to breathe".

Duration: initially "last few weeks" then clarified as "maybe even longer... might have even coincided with that job a couple of months ago" and "More like two months, I would say"—consistent with several weeks to ~2 months.
Onset with job: "I also started a new job slightly recently. It might have even coincided with that job a couple of months ago" and patient confirms job started about two months ago.

Difficulty waking/low energy: "getting up in the morning is really difficult" and "I don't have much energy at all during the day"; trouble sleeping: "it's more like I'm just having trouble sleeping at all".
Reduced appetite: "I'm not eating very much at the moment."

Lower mood and difficulty focusing are supported ("my mood is lower recently"; "Finding it really hard to... keep focusing"), but the patient does not state general disinterest in activities; disinterest is specified only regarding sex drive: "just over the last few months, just been disinterested" (in marital/sexual context). Extending disinterest to activities broadly is additional.

Shortness of breath with exertion and reduced tolerance: "when I've been doing sports as well, I find sometimes it's quite difficult to breathe. So I have some kind of like shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago" indicating reduced exercise tolerance.
No vision change: "Any change in your vision?" – "No, no, nothing like that."
Denies self-harm/harm to others: "Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or harming anyone else?" – "No, no, no, not really."
History of hypothyroidism: "in the past I have a history of hypothyroidism... Hypo. Hypothyroidism" confirmed by patient and clinician.

The transcript clearly states the history of hypothyroidism once; mentioning that it appears again in a subjective section is documentation structure, not a new clinical claim, so it is consistent and supported by "I have a history of hypothyroidism".
Similarly, the note stating hypothyroidism on levothyroxine in an assessment section is based on supported history: "I have a history of hypothyroidism" and ongoing thyroxine use.
Ongoing thyroxine: "I have a drug history of thyroxine" and to "Do you continue to take thyroxine now?" – "Yes."
Ongoing nature: Directly confirmed by "Do you continue to take thyroxine now?" – "Yes" and "So you're taking thyroxine at the moment?" – "Yes."
No medication allergies: "Any drug? Allergies?..." – "No, I have no medication. Allergies?" and clinician repeats "No allergies." Absence in a header is consistent.
Allergies documented as none in another section aligns with the explicit statement: "No, I have no medication. Allergies?" and "No allergies."
Father suicide ~15 years ago: "my father has committed suicide about 15 years ago."
Same content rephrased: "my father has committed suicide about 15 years ago."

No other psychiatric illnesses: Clinician asks about other family psychiatric history and depression; patient implies none: "Is there any other significant family history... No, no depression or anything like that? Running in family..." and there is no contrary statement.
Marital status: "Yeah, I'm married. I've been for many years."
Duration married: same quote, "Yeah, I'm married. I've been for many years."

Symptoms and duration are supported, but the stated differential diagnosis ("mood disorder and thyroid-related or other medical etiologies") is not discussed in the transcript; the clinician only mentions doing tests and examination without naming differentials.

Decreased appetite and reduced libido are supported, but linking them explicitly as mood-consistent and planning to "screen for depressive illness and evaluate thyroid function" is not stated. The transcript only mentions doing blood tests and an exam, without specifying depression screening or thyroid focus.
Dyspnea on exertion with decreased tolerance: "when I've been doing sports... quite difficult to breathe... shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago."

History of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine is supported, but the need to assess thyroid function and adjust dose is not explicitly stated. The clinician only generally proposes "some blood tests" and "investigations" without specifying thyroid or dose adjustment.

Family history and current suicidality: Father suicide: "my father has committed suicide about 15 years ago"; current status: "Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or harming anyone else?" – "No, no, no, not really" and at the end "I'm glad you're, you know, although you have a low mood, you're not feeling suicidal, just to confirm that."

In-person visit with GP in next few days: "I would like to probably see you in person... do an examination and also we probably like to do some blood tests" and "do you think it'd be possible to... book an appointment in the next few days with your GP... That would be ideal."
Specific labs (CBC, CMP, TSH, Free T4, HbA1c, B12) are never mentioned. Only generic "some blood tests" and "investigations" are discussed.
Reviewing/adjusting thyroxine dose based on thyroid panel is not stated; only generic blood tests and examination are planned.
The clinician confirms absence of suicidal thoughts but does not describe a formal safety assessment or safety plan if symptoms worsen. That language is not present.
No mention of sleep hygiene advice or formal sleep assessment planning appears in the transcript.
There is no discussion of nutrition/hydration guidance or referral for dietary counseling, despite reduced appetite being noted.
No explicit follow-up interval (2–4 weeks or otherwise) is given. Only the next few days GP appointment is discussed.
There is no mention of possible pulmonary or cardiac evaluation, spirometry, or imaging; only general further investigations via GP are discussed.
No specific follow-up timeframe (2–4 weeks) or red-flag-based return instructions are stated in the transcript.
Sleep: "getting up in the morning is really difficult" and later "it's more like I'm just having trouble sleeping at all"; he clarifies he is not waking early but has general trouble sleeping.
Lower mood and focus: "my mood is lower recently"; "Finding it really hard to... keep focusing"; clinician summarizes "you've had difficulty focusing... your mood has been slightly lower."
Fatigue and difficulty with usual activities: "I don't have much energy at all during the day. Often... doing most things that I would normally find easy, it's become quite difficult."
Appetite: "I'm not eating very much at the moment."

Decreased libido: "my mood is lower recently and so I like my sex drive has kind of decreased over the past few months" and "just over the last few months, just been disinterested" (in sexual context).

Shortness of breath with exertion and reduced tolerance: "when I've been doing sports... quite difficult to breathe" and "shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago."
Vision: "Any change in your vision?" – "No, no, nothing like that."

Self-harm/harm to others: "Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or harming anyone else?" – "No, no, no, not really." and later confirmed "although you have a low mood, you're not feeling suicidal, just to confirm that."
